notes: PSA 5.3 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.09. Prostate volume 58 mL. DRE suspicious. csPCa 0.79.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer diagnosis following recent biopsy and MRI findings.

Recently retired firefighter with a history of upper abdominal surgery. He is married but lives alone, with his adult son as primary contact. He is a current smoker with a 23 pack-year history, abstains from alcohol, and cycles 5 times a week for commuting. His IPSS score is 2/35, indicating mild lower urinary tract symptoms. He has had recent appointments for gastroenterology surveillance colonoscopy, vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins, and dental check-ups. PSA trend shows an increase from 2.8 ng/mL in May 2022 to 5.3 ng/mL in February 2025.
On digital rectal examination, a suspicious nodule is palpated in the left peripheral zone, consistent with clinical stage cTx. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs.
